findings.title: Calling non-existent no-arg method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() causes compilation failure
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but its superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only defines `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` taking a `UserModel` parameter. This causes a compilation error (`cannot find symbol: method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`).

findings.title: Conditional passkeys are disabled on initial login when user is null
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both `authenticate()` (line 115) and `challenge()` (line 137) gate `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` on this method. During a normal initial login, `context.getUser()` is `null`, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` always evaluates to `false`, completely disabling conditional UI passkeys whenever the user has not yet been identified. Additionally, when `user != null` (e.g. re-authentication), it does not check whether the identified user actually has a passkey credential configured (`webauthnAuth.configuredFor(context.getSession(), context.getRealm(), user)`), so passkey UI elements will be rendered even for users without a passkey.
